patient.chief_complaint: Acute onset diplopia, ataxia, and inability to walk in a 28-year-old, with no limb weakness but complete areflexia.
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. D. is a 28-year-old previously healthy man presenting to the emergency department with a 4-day history of progressive neurological symptoms. Three weeks prior, he had a mild upper respiratory illness lasting 5 days. Four days ago, he noticed horizontal double vision that worsened rapidly. By day 2, he developed drooping of both eyelids. On day 3, he noticed severe balance problems — he fell twice and has been holding walls to walk. He denies any limb weakness: his arms and legs feel strong. He denies any headache, vomiting, or confusion. He has no back pain. He denies any recent travel or tick exposure. Emergency providers initially suspected a posterior fossa stroke given the ophthalmoplegia and ataxia. Brain CT was unremarkable. On examination, the striking finding is the triad of complete ophthalmoplegia, severe ataxia, and complete areflexia in an otherwise healthy 28-year-old with normal limb strength.

results.title: Anti-GQ1b antibody–associated cranial polyneuropathy: ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and areflexia phenotype
results.finding: Anti-GQ1b IgG antibody has sensitivity >95% for the ophthalmoplegia-ataxia-areflexia cranial polyneuropathy phenotype. The clinical course is typically self-limiting, with most patients recovering within weeks to months.

results.title: Anti-GQ1b cranial polyneuropathy with limb-weakness overlap
results.finding: A subset of patients with the anti-GQ1b cranial polyneuropathy phenotype develop concurrent limb weakness; this overlap form has been reported in approximately 10–20% of cases in case series.

results.title: Anti-GQ1b antibodies in related conditions
results.finding: Anti-GQ1b IgG has also been detected in Bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis. Neuroimaging is typically performed to evaluate for structural lesions in patients presenting with ophthalmoplegia and ataxia.

output.summary: Retrieved evidence covers anti-GQ1b IgG–associated cranial/sensory syndromes: the antibody has high reported sensitivity for the ophthalmoplegia-ataxia-areflexia phenotype, an overlap form with limb weakness is described in a minority of case-series patients, and the same antibody appears in Bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis. Published evidence supports IVIG and plasmapheresis as therapeutic options for these conditions, with a generally favorable prognosis. Clinical correlation with individual patient findings is required.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Miller Fisher syndrome (GBS variant), anti-GQ1b positive

differential.key_features: Anti-GQ1b positive in both, but BBE includes altered consciousness or hyperreflexia — absent here, with preserved alertness and complete areflexia favouring MFS.
Must be excluded by MRI given ophthalmoplegia and ataxia; classically asymmetric, with crossed findings; MFS pattern is bilateral and symmetric with global areflexia.
Triad of ophthalmoplegia / ataxia / confusion; mental status is preserved, no risk factors for thiamine deficiency.
Ptosis and diplopia possible but reflexes preserved and no fatigability; AChR antibodies negative expected.
Descending paralysis with bulbar onset; cholinergic signs absent here; sensory paresthesias are present in this patient.

optimal_actions.action: Obtain CBC, CMP, HIV, anti-GM1/anti-GQ1b ganglioside antibodies, and stool culture / Campylobacter serology if recent diarrhea
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Mild leukocytosis / elevated inflammatory markers reflecting antecedent infection; ganglioside antibodies for variant typing; trigger identification (Campylobacter, CMV, EBV, Mycoplasma, HIV)

optimal_actions.action: Order nerve conduction studies and needle EMG (EMG/NCS)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Demyelinating pattern (prolonged DML, conduction block, reduced CV, absent F-waves) consistent with AIDP, or reduced CMAP amplitudes in axonal variants (AMAN/AMSAN)

optimal_actions.action: Perform lumbar puncture for CSF analysis
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Albuminocytologic dissociation — elevated protein with cell count <10/μL; may be normal in the first week of illness

optimal_actions.action: Order bedside respiratory function testing (FVC, MIP/MEP, NIF) and repeat every 4–6 hours
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Baseline and serial FVC, MIP/MEP, NIF; deterioration to FVC <20 mL/kg, MIP worse than -30 cmH2O, or VC <40% predicted triggers ICU transfer / intubation

optimal_actions.action: Search the medical literature for IVIG vs plasma exchange evidence to guide disease-modifying therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: IVIG (0.4 g/kg/day x 5 days) and plasma exchange are equivalently effective first-line therapies; combination not superior

optimal_actions.action: Check drug interactions / contraindications for IVIG (renal function, IgA deficiency screen) and/or plasma exchange (coagulation, calcium, hemodynamics)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirmation that IVIG can be given safely (no severe renal impairment, no IgA deficiency) or that plasma exchange is appropriate (adequate vascular access, stable coagulation)

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sinus tachycardia or bradycardia; conduction or repolarisation abnormalities reflecting autonomic involvement

optimal_actions.action: Start continuous inpatient cardiac telemetry for the period of maximal weakness and keep it running alongside serial respiratory function. Autonomic instability affects about two thirds of patients and is a leading cause of in-hospital death: bradyarrhythmias, pauses beyond 3 seconds and blood-pressure lability are what trigger ICU escalation
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Normal sinus rhythm throughout. Rare isolated PVCs — the recording is read for the bradyarrhythmias, pauses beyond 3 seconds and blood-pressure lability that trigger ICU escalation

useless_tools.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Functional / metabolic brain imaging adds no value in a peripheral demyelinating syndrome.
Cerebrovascular imaging is not indicated in a peripheral neuropathy without focal cerebral signs.

sequence_constraints.reason: Document respiratory status (FVC/NIF) before committing to IVIG vs plasma exchange — severe respiratory compromise mandates ICU triage and may influence treatment choice and timing.
Renal function, IgA screen, and CBC must be reviewed before IVIG to mitigate renal failure, anaphylaxis (IgA-deficient patients), and aseptic meningitis risk.

critical_actions: Obtain MRI brain with brainstem sequences to rule out brainstem stroke / BBE given ophthalmoplegia and ataxia.
Order anti-GQ1b IgG and broader ganglioside panel as part of variant typing.
Initiate IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (or plasma exchange) — both effective in MFS.
Monitor respiratory function (FVC, NIF) — extension to GBS with limb weakness is possible.
Continuous cardiac telemetry for autonomic dysrhythmias.
contraindicated_actions: Do not start corticosteroids as monotherapy.
Do not delay treatment awaiting anti-GQ1b results — they take days to return and treatment is time-sensitive.
key_reasoning_points: Classic MFS triad: ophthalmoplegia + ataxia + areflexia with preserved alertness — the absence of weakness distinguishes from typical GBS.
Anti-GQ1b IgG is the serological hallmark (>90% sensitivity in MFS) and supports clinical diagnosis.
Brainstem MRI is recommended despite the typical syndrome to exclude posterior-circulation stroke and Bickerstaff encephalitis.
Overlap syndromes (MFS extending to GBS or BBE) occur — monitor for progression to limb weakness, bulbar dysfunction, or altered consciousness.

red_herrings.data_point: Normal cell counts with elevated CSF protein
red_herrings.intended_effect: Reassure that no infectious encephalitis is present and anchor on a benign process.
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Albuminocytologic dissociation is the expected CSF profile in MFS as in classic GBS and supports the diagnosis.
